neighbours.label: The token ' wool'/' Wool' wherever it stands, including names built on it (Woolf, Woolworths, Woolcock) and 'woolly'; vs other fibres, 'wolf', and wool-related words without the token
fire: Leonard Woolf ran the Hogarth Press with his wife from their home.
The museum displays a reconstructed skeleton of a woolly rhinoceros.
She stopped at Woolworths on the way home to buy milk.
In the corner sat a heap of wool waiting to be carded and spun.
The Woolcock Institute studies sleep and breathing disorders.
He wore a thick wool sweater against the mountain wind.
Herds of woolly mammoths roamed the northern steppes during the last ice age.
The mill bought raw wool from farmers across the valley.
quiet: Leonard Bernstein conducted the orchestra for many years.
The museum displays a reconstructed skeleton of a giant ground sloth.
She stopped at the corner shop on the way home to buy milk.
In the corner sat a heap of cotton waiting to be cleaned and spun.
The Wellcome Institute studies the history of medicine.
He wore a thick fleece jacket against the mountain wind.
Herds of grey wolves roamed the northern steppes during the last ice age.
The mill bought raw linen from farmers across the valley.

predictions: Sentences with the ' wool'/' Wool' token reach 0.5-0.85 (lower when 'wool' ends a phrase plainly); cotton, wolf, fleece and 'Wolfe' stay under 0.2; sheep may reach about 0.35.
notes: Card: ' wool' x18, ' Wool' x11, '毛' x3 of the top 32 (Woolf, Woolcock, Woolen Mills, woolly mammoth, bag of wool). Probe: Woolworths 0.848, woolly mammoth 0.720, Virginia Woolf 0.686, 羊毛 0.461; but 'soft merino wool.' only 0.175; cotton 0.150, wolf 0.119, sheep/fleece 0.351.
